description: Job Summary The Senior Buyer is responsible for the strategic sourcing, negotiation, and procurement of fabricated and machined aerospace components. This role requires a deep understanding of aerospace materials, manufacturing processes, and supply base management to ensure quality, cost, and delivery objectives are met. The Senior Buyer will work cross-functionally with Engineering, Quality, Planning, and suppliers to support both development and production programs. This role will also lead supplier performance mitigation strategies and collaborate closely with Planning to ensure material requirements are accurately understood and met on time. JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Source, negotiate, and manage purchase orders for fabricated and machined aerospace parts, including precision components, assemblies, and subassemblies. Develop and maintain relationships with key suppliers to ensure consistent performance in cost, quality, and delivery. Collaborate with Engineering and Manufacturing teams to understand technical requirements and translate them into sourcing strategies. Work closely with Planning to ensure material requirements are accurately communicated, understood, and met by suppliers in alignment with production schedules. Read and interpret technical drawings, specifications, and bill of materials (BOMs) to validate supplier capability and quote accuracy. Conduct supplier evaluations, including capacity, capability, and risk assessments. Lead and execute supplier performance mitigation strategies for underperforming vendors, including creation of recovery plans, risk assessments, and dual/multi-sourcing strategies. Monitor supplier performance using scorecards and KPIs; identify performance gaps and initiate corrective actions in collaboration with Quality and Operations teams. Engage in root cause analysis and continuous improvement efforts with suppliers to address recurring quality or delivery issues. Support new product introduction (NPI) by sourcing prototypes and transitioning to production suppliers. Negotiate and manage long-term agreements (LTAs), supplier contracts, and terms & conditions. Stay informed of market trends, commodity pricing, and geopolitical factors that may affect supply. Maintain ERP/MRP system accuracy for pricing, lead times, delivery dates, and supplier data integrity. Ensure timely delivery of materials and proactive resolution of potential supply chain disruptions. JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or related field. 5–10 years of procurement experience in the aerospace industry, specifically with machined and fabricated parts. Strong understanding of CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, and finishing processes. Proven ability to read and understand engineering drawings and GD&T. Experience with AS9100 requirements and aerospace supplier quality systems. Strong negotiation, contract management, and supplier relationship management skills. Demonstrated success in mitigating supplier performance risks and improving supply continuity. Experience working closely with Planning, Production Control, or Materials Management to align supply and demand. Proficiency in ERP/MRP systems; Epicor Kinetic experience a plus . Knowledge of ITAR, DFARS, and other regulatory requirements APICS, CPM, or CPSM certification (preferred). PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS & WORKING CONDITIONS While performing the duties of this job, employees are regularly required to sit, walk and stand; talk or hear, both in person and by telephone; use their hands repetitively to finger, handle, feel or operate standard office equipment; reach with hands and arms; and lift up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, and the ability to adjust focus. The work environment characteristics described here represent those employee encounters while performing this job's essential functions. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions. Employees work under typical office conditions, and the noise level is usually quiet to moderate. However, in certain assignments, an employee may work near moving equipment and be exposed to toxic or caustic chemicals, biological hazards, airborne fumes, outdoor weather conditions, and loud, prolonged noise. description: Description Looking to join a passionate team dedicated to developing and manufacturing life-saving biopharmaceuticals? Avid Bioservices is a leading clinical and commercial biologics CDMO focused on creating innovative solutions to meet the needs of our clients and improve patient outcomes. Your Role: The Senior Procurement Specialist drives the organization's sourcing lifecycle to optimize costs, mitigate market risks, and guarantee supply continuity. This role balances strategic category leadership with execution, managing a diverse portfolio across both direct procurement (production-critical raw materials and inventory) and indirect procurement (operational goods, software, and corporate services). The ideal candidate acts as a strategic advisor to stakeholders and builds resilient, high-performing supplier networks. Key Responsibilities: Process purchase orders, track deliveries, and ensure timely receipt of goods Responsible for negotiating preferred/discount pricing or contract pricing with vendors. Maintain strong relationships with suppliers, monitor performance, and resolve disputes or claims. Partners with AP to resolve vendor invoice issues. Partners with MSAT to drive second sourcing activities for raw materials. Helps with obtaining vendor documentation for RMS updates for materials. Drive sourcing strategies for raw materials and core engineering components to ensure milestones are being met. Complex Contracting: Draft and negotiating complex, multi-year Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Help drive Key Performance Metrics (KPI’s) such as cost savings/avoidance, supplier performance and reduction in procurement cycle times. Managing high-value corporate spend categories (e.g., Enterprise Software, Global Facilities, Professional Services) and aligning procurement with executive business goals. Responsible for executing and managing enterprise-wide sourcing strategies for non-production goods and services. This role focuses on optimizing corporate spend, driving structural cost reduction initiatives, and building resilient supplier frameworks across high value spend categories. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Finance, or a related technical field. 5 to 8+ years of indirect/direct corporate procurement or category management experience. Experience with ERP / inventory control systems required, Dynamics D365 experience preferred. Excellent stakeholder management, communication and influencing skills. Preferred Qualifications: Professional certification (e.g., CPSM, MCIPS, or APICS/CSCP) is highly preferred. cGMP experience and writing SOP’s and contracts highly preferred. Elite negotiation skills with a proven track record of securing multi-million-dollar annual savings. Position Type/Expected Hours of Work: This role is a full-time onsite position in Tustin, CA. Days and hours of work are Monday through Friday 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. unless otherwise stated by Supervisor. The employee must also have the ability to work overtime and/or weekends when necessary. Compensation: We offer competitive compensation packages for this role, including a base salary, performance-based bonuses, and comprehensive benefits such as health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) matching, and paid time off. The compensation range for this role is $24.23 - $30.28 hourly depending on experience and qualifications. Additionally, we offer opportunities for career growth and development as well as a supportive and inclusive work environment. Who you are: You have a "bring it on!" team player approach and an unshakable positive attitude, always ready to tackle anything that comes your way. Your written and verbal skills are out of this world, and you communicate with clarity and confidence. You have exceptional multitasking skills and an unparalleled attention to detail that ensure the smooth running of everything. You are a master at building relationships, capable of establishing connections with anyone, be it team members, clients, vendors, or suppliers. Physical Demands & Work Environment: In this dynamic role, expect a blend of regular activities like sitting, standing, and walking, with occasional physically engaging tasks such as lifting objects up to 25 pounds. The work environment might expose you to electrical shocks, toxic chemicals, vibrations, or loud noise levels occasionally. However, reasonable accommodations are available to enable individuals with different abilities to perform effectively, ensuring a supportive and adaptable work setting. Your visual acuity, including close, distance, and color vision, will be essential in navigating through the diverse day-to-day demands of this position.

description: Beehive Industries is dedicated to Powering American Defense by revolutionizing the design, development, and delivery of jet propulsion systems to support the warfighter. Through the integration of additive manufacturing, the company aims to meet the growing and urgent needs for unmanned aerial defense by dramatically improving a jet engine’s speed to market, fuel efficiency, and cost. Founded in 2020, the company is headquartered in Centennial, Colorado, with additional facilities in Knoxville, Tennessee, Loveland Ohio, and Mount Vernon, Ohio. Beehive is committed to grow and advance the defense industrial base while manufacturing exclusively in the USA. This role will be located at our Cincinnati, Ohio facility. Role Overview We are seeking a highly motivated and detail-oriented Buyer to own and support execution of all outside processing and special process requirements in a fast-paced aerospace and defense environment. This role owns the supplier relationship and purchasing process for outside services including non-destructive testing, heat treatment, and other specialized manufacturing services The Buyer works closely with Manufacturing, Quality, Engineering, Supply Planning, and Program teams to ensure outside processing is completed in accordance with purchase order requirements, customer specifications, applicable aerospace standards, and required delivery schedules. This position is responsible for negotiating long term agreements, understanding supplier capacity and constraints, partnering with technical teams to qualify new sources and managing the complete outside-service process from purchase requisition through supplier execution. What You’ll Do... Manage purchase orders and supplier relationships for all assigned outside processing and special process requirements. Manage RFQs/RFPs, supplier selection, bid analysis, negotiations, and contract execution. Ensure full compliance with FAR/DFARS requirements and all government contracting regulations throughout the procurement process. Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Quality, Finance, and Program Management teams to support business objectives. Negotiate pricing, payment terms, lead times, service agreements, and long-term supply arrangements. Develop and maintain supplier relationships to ensure performance in quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness. Identify and execute cost reduction, process improvement, and supply chain risk mitigation initiatives. Maintain accurate procurement records, purchase orders, and sourcing documentation within ERP/MRP systems. Support audits and documentation requirements related to AS9100, ISO standards, and government contracting compliance. Own supplier delivery performance for outside processing requirements and proactively manage material through the supplier network. Coordinate shipment of material to and from outside processors to support production schedules. Monitor supplier lead times, work-in-process, capacity constraints, and potential delivery risks. Support long-term agreements, pricing agreements, blanket purchase orders, and other commercial strategies where appropriate You have... Education Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or related field preferred. Experience 3–7+ years of purchasing or procurement experience in manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or highly regulated industries. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience preparing, managing, and auditing procurement compliance documentation. Strong negotiation, analytical, and supplier management skills. Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems Ability to read and interpret statements of work, and technical specifications Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and procurement analytics. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment. The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance Nice to have... Experience in aerospace, defense, precision machining, additive, or advanced manufacturing environments. Experience supporting lean manufacturing or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience with long-term supply agreements and logistics Experience with ERP/MRP systems such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar. If this sounds like you, please submit an application with your resume. This could be the opportunity you are looking for to expand your skills, contribute to a winning team, and work with talented people who love what they do and take pride in our mission. Beehive Industries offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes group Medical, Dental, Life, and Short and Long-Term disability coverage from day one. We also offer a generous 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan with a Company match. Every role at Beehive Industries is bonus eligible and will also receive equity in the company. Beehive Industries is committed to full compliance with applicable anti-discrimination laws. We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We strive to create an inclusive work environment and will not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

description: About Blue Bird Corporation Blue Bird (NASDAQ: BLBD) is recognized as a technology leader and innovator of school buses since its founding in 1927. Our dedicated team members design, engineer and manufacture school buses with a singular focus on safety, reliability, and durability. School buses carry the most precious cargo in the world – 25 million children twice a day – making them the most trusted mode of student transportation. The company is the proven leader in low- and zero-emission school buses with more than 25,000 propane, natural gas, and electric powered buses sold. Blue Bird is transforming the student transportation industry through cleaner energy solutions. For more information on Blue Bird’s complete product and service portfolio, visit www.blue-bird.com. JOB SUMMARY: Reporting to the Senior Manager, Purchasing, the Senior Buyer, Powertrain & Chassis Systems is responsible for leading the strategic sourcing, contract negotiation, and operational lifecycle management for powertrain, chassis, and assigned heavy mechanical and structural commodities. This role serves as the primary commercial and operational owner for critical components and systems, including engine and powertrain systems, transmissions and driveline, steering, braking, suspension, axles, wheels and tires, and assigned structural/mechanical systems. The position balances long-term cost optimization and supplier relationship management with aggressive hands-on risk mitigation, serving as the ultimate escalation point for production shortages, supplier recovery, and supply continuity planning to ensure uninterrupted vehicle assembly. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Commodity Strategy & Sourcing: Develop and execute comprehensive sourcing strategies for the Powertrain & Chassis Systems portfolio to optimize total cost of ownership (TCO), quality, and delivery. Supplier Risk & Crisis Management: Lead operational risk management, serve as the primary escalation point for critical chassis component shortages, and establish cross-functional crisis management teams to resolve supplier delivery failures. Contract & Cost Negotiation: Lead multi-million-dollar contract negotiations, long-term agreements (LTAs), and pricing reviews with major tier-1 automotive and heavy-duty commercial vehicle suppliers. Supplier Performance & Technical Recovery: Monitor On-Time Delivery (OTD) and quality governance; lead 8D root-cause investigations and corrective action plans directly with supplier manufacturing plants when quality or delivery targets are missing. Capacity & Vulnerability Mapping: Conduct regular supplier capacity reviews, tooling and manufacturing assessments, sub-tier dependency reviews, and vulnerability mapping to identify capacity constraints, long-lead components, and other supply continuity risks. Program Launch & Supplier Transition: Lead purchasing activities supporting new product introduction and supplier transition, including sourcing readiness, commercial closure, tooling, capacity validation, APQP/PPAP execution, early supplier engagement (ESI), and production launch readiness. Resilience Planning: Drive dual-sourcing and manufacturing contingency initiatives for high-risk, single-sourced components and systems. Operational Discipline: Develop KPI dashboards, manage material cost variance reporting, and mentor junior buyers and operational specialists within the purchasing team. REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES: Strong knowledge of automotive or commercial vehicle powertrain, chassis, driveline, and/or heavy mechanical systems. Advanced Sourcing & Negotiation: Proven track record of managing high-spend portfolios, executing complex supplier agreements, and navigating raw material (steel/aluminum) indexing. Operational Recovery: Demonstrated experience leading supplier recovery efforts and managing business continuity in high-pressure manufacturing environments. Quality & Engineering Literacy: Strong understanding of automotive quality standards, APQP, PPAP, blueprint reading, and geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T). Influence & Collaboration: Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders (Engineering, Quality, Operations) without direct authority. Systems Proficiency: High proficiency in ERP systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, or Infor) and advanced Microsoft Excel data analysis capabilities. description: Your role The Strategic Sourcing role is accountable for developing and executing a sustainable procurement strategy within their assigned commodity area. This includes establishing and managing long‑term agreements and service‑level commitments, optimising and rationalising the supplier base, and ensuring effective supplier onboarding. A key focus of the role is strengthening supply chain resilience by building. As Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager - Supplier Development, you will execute sourcing strategies that secure qualified capacity for production ramp-up and build a competitive, resilient supply base. You will lead supplier selection, negotiation, onboarding, qualification coordination, launch readiness, and performance, with particular focus on new product introduction, dual sourcing, and continuity of supply. This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Manager reflects accountability for sourcing strategies, supplier relationships, spend, contracts, risk, and results. What You Will Do Develop category and supplier strategies aligned with growth, NPI, production ramp-up, cost, capacity, quality, and supply-resilience priorities. Lead market analysis, RFIs, RFQs and RFPs, total-cost evaluation, negotiations, supplier selection, awards, and agreements. Assess suppliers for capability, capacity, processes, quality systems, financial health, scalability, compliance, and risk. Coordinate supplier onboarding and qualification across Engineering, Supplier Quality, Operations, Planning, Finance, and other functions, with clear milestones, owners, risks, and escalations. Facilitate product and part qualification, including specifications, samples, tooling, first articles, validation, deviation closure, approvals, and production release. Engineering and Quality own technical requirements, validation decisions, and formal approval; you drive supplier response, timing, commercial readiness, escalation, and completion. Secure capacity and launch readiness through reviews, forecasts, lead-time and flexibility commitments, inventory plans, and commercial agreements. Build dual-source and continuity plans for critical parts and single-source risks, coordinating alternate-source qualification with technical and quality teams. Lead supplier reviews, performance improvement, and recovery plans covering quality, delivery, capacity, cost, compliance, and risk. Deliver savings, cost avoidance, working-capital improvement, productivity, and total-cost benefits without compromising quality or continuity. Develop supplier relationships that improve access to capacity, technology, and innovation while meeting legal, ethical, sustainability, and Atlas Copco requirements. To succeed, you will need Typically 5-8 years of experience in strategic sourcing, category management, supplier development, procurement, or supply chain, preferably in engineered products or manufacturing. Success sourcing, negotiating with, qualifying, onboarding, and ramping suppliers for NPI or production growth. Experience coordinating suppliers and cross-functional teams through qualification and production release. Strong negotiation, contract management, cost analysis, total-cost, supplier-performance, and risk-management capabilities. Ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, bills of material, manufacturing processes, and supplier-capability information. Strong communication, influence, judgment, analytical problem-solving, and project leadership without formal authority. Bachelor's degree in supply chain, engineering, business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Location and travel: This position may be remote within the United States or hybrid; residence near Saugerties, New York, is not required. Approximately 40% travel is expected, primarily to supplier sites for qualification, launch readiness, business reviews, improvement, and issue resolution, and to company locations. Travel will be mainly within North America, with international travel as needed. Arrangements are subject to company policy, employment eligibility, payroll and tax requirements, and business needs. In return, we offer Culture of trust and accountability Lifelong learning and career growth Innovation powered by people Comprehensive compensation and benefits 401k Automatic Company Contribution and match Generous PTO package Annual Variable Compensation Program Salary: $125,000-$150,000/yr Job location This position may be remote within the United States or hybrid; residence near Saugerties, New York, is not required. Contact information Talent Acquisition Team: Kasey Griffin Uniting curious minds Behind every innovative solution, there are people working together to transform the future. With careers sparked by initiative and lifelong learning, we unite curious minds, and you could be one of them.
